answer: The September 2025 provision stock still embeds material caution; the low FY25 charge does not show a completed normalisation. The $424m charge (5bps of average loans, versus $537m/7bps in FY24) reconciles as gross loss flow of $969m (write-offs $561m plus new IAPs $408m) less $545m of offsets (write-backs $195m, recoveries $247m, other changes in CAP $103m). Gross loss emergence did not fall much - net write-offs to average loans rose to 6bps from 5bps and new impaired inflows rose 19% to $831m - so the lower charge rests partly on non-recurring recoveries and write-backs. On the stock side, total ECL fell only 2% to $4,987m: the modelled CAP released $168m on better commercial-property, interest-rate and delinquency outlooks, but management offset this with a 5ppt increase in the downside scenario weight to 47.5% (upside cut to 2.5%), overlays up $59m YoY (and $108m half-on-half) to $238m for portfolio seasoning and stressed geographies, and IAPs flat at $539m (the $72m HoH fall was a single-name trade-sector write-off). The scenario disclosure quantifies the caution: reported probability-weighted ECL of $4,987m sits $1.9bn above 100% base-case ECL of $3,040m and $2.2bn below 100% downside ECL of $7,152m, against a severe downside (unemployment peak 11%, commercial property -32%). The counterweight is that coverage ratios drifted down - provisions to gross loans 58bps from 63bps, CAP to credit RWA 1.25% from 1.30%, impaired coverage 39.5% from 41.3% - so the stock did not keep pace with 6% loan growth, and part of the metric improvement is definitional (serviceability-treatment change for mortgage delinquencies, auto-portfolio sale for consumer). Judgment: credit quality genuinely improved (stressed exposures 1.28% of TCE from 1.45%), but management's own actions - a 47.5% downside weight, higher overlays, a $1.9bn buffer above base case - show normalisation is not declared complete. The release of that caution remains a future P&L tailwind, not a delivered one.

limitations: The documents do not quantify in dollars the CAP impact of the 5ppt downside-weight increase; the $103m 'other changes in CAP' benefit is not decomposed across its four stated drivers.
Overlay composition is described only qualitatively; dollar amounts per overlay theme (seasoning, geographies, releases) are not disclosed.
No prior-period figure for the gap between reported ECL and 100% base-case ECL is given, so whether the $1.9bn buffer grew or shrank versus September 2024 cannot be verified from these documents.
The $247m of recoveries is not split between debt-sale proceeds and collections, so its repeatability cannot be assessed.
The delinquency impact of the mortgage serviceability-treatment change is not quantified, so the split between genuine and definitional improvement is unknown.
